cases.question: In anyio.to_thread.run_sync, how does an explicit cancellable=False interact with abandon_on_cancel=True, when is the deprecation warning emitted, and what exact arguments are delegated to run_sync_in_worker_thread?
cases.expected_answer: Any non-None cancellable value overrides abandon_on_cancel, so explicit False wins over True. The same non-None branch emits DeprecationWarning with stacklevel=2. It awaits get_async_backend().run_sync_in_worker_thread(func,args,abandon_on_cancel=abandon_on_cancel,limiter=limiter) and returns that result. None leaves abandon_on_cancel unchanged and does not warn.

cases.question: Compare fail_after and move_on_after: how do they compute deadlines for a numeric delay versus None, which calls receive shield and reason, and what exact condition in fail_at raises TimeoutError?
cases.expected_answer: fail_after captures the backend clock and computes current_time()+delay for a numeric delay or math.inf for None. It enters fail_at(deadline,shield=shield,reason=reason) and yields that scope. move_on_after uses the backend clock only for a numeric delay, otherwise math.inf, and directly returns create_cancel_scope(deadline=deadline,shield=shield). fail_at normalizes a None deadline to infinity, yields the created cancel scope, then raises TimeoutError only when cancelled_caught and current_time()>=cancel_scope.deadline are both true; it includes reason only when truthy.
required_details: Both numeric delays become current backend time plus delay
None delays become math.inf
fail_after delegates deadline, shield and reason to fail_at and yields its scope
move_on_after directly returns a backend cancel scope with deadline and shield
fail_at creates and yields a backend cancel scope with normalized deadline and shield
TimeoutError requires cancelled_caught AND current time at least scope.deadline after exiting the scope
Truthy reason becomes TimeoutError message; falsy reason yields bare TimeoutError

cases.question: In _multicall, in which order are implementations called, how does firstresult handle None versus non-None results, and when does a missing required caller argument become HookCallError?
cases.expected_answer: It iterates reversed(hook_impls). For ordinary non-wrapper implementations it appends only non-None results and breaks only after a non-None result when firstresult is true. firstresult returns results[0] or None; otherwise it returns the list. Building positional args from caller_kwargs for required argnames catches KeyError and raises HookCallError mentioning the missing name, chained from that KeyError; the outer exception path still runs teardown before propagation.
required_details: Iteration uses reversed(hook_impls)
For ordinary implementations None is excluded and does not stop firstresult calls
Non-None results are appended; firstresult then breaks
firstresult returns first collected value or None, otherwise the result list
Required positional arguments are looked up by hook_impl.argnames in caller_kwargs
Missing required lookup KeyError becomes HookCallError chained from that KeyError
The outer exception path preserves teardown before final propagation

cases.question: How do HookCaller.call_historic and HookCaller._maybe_apply_history record and replay calls for a new hook implementation, and what arguments and callback values are used?
cases.expected_answer: call_historic asserts history exists, normalizes kwargs, applies defaults, verifies required arguments and appends (kwargs,result_callback) before execution. It invokes _hookexec(self.name,self._hookimpls.copy(),kwargs,False), protecting iteration from plugin registration changes. With no callback it returns; for list results it calls the callback for each element. _maybe_apply_history acts only on historic hooks, iterates stored entries, and invokes _hookexec(self.name,[method],kwargs,False) for the single new implementation. If res is truthy and callback not None, it asserts list and passes res[0].
required_details: Normalizes kwargs, applies defaults and verifies required arguments before recording
Appends kwargs and result_callback to history before execution
Initial dispatch uses name, a COPY of hookimpls, kwargs, and firstresult=False
Initial callback receives each list result; no callback returns without callback invocation
Replay only runs when the hook is historic
Replay dispatch uses a SINGLE new method with stored kwargs and firstresult=False
Replay callback requires truthy result and non-None callback, then receives res[0]
